thread:
maria: Heads-up — seeing intermittent ClassCastException in Kotlin client while streaming NDJSON responses. Two services, both use our kotlin-client built with shaded deps.

alex: Can you paste the stacktrace and the client config you used?

maria: Stacktrace (trimmed):
```
java.lang.ClassCastException: com.google.gson.internal.bind.ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory$Adapter cannot be cast to com.google.gson.TypeAdapter	at com.redwood.client.JsonStreamParser.parse(JsonStreamParser.kt:42)	at com.redwood.client.OkHttpBodyHandler.handleStream(OkHttpBodyHandler.kt:88)
```
Client snippet:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .cookieJar(JavaNetCookieJar(cookieManager))
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider))
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build()
// gson is pulled from our shaded-sdk jar
val gson = Gson()
```
Also gradle deps: we shadowed com.google.gson into com.redwood.shaded.gson via shadowJar relocations.

jess: quick thought — have you tried disabling connection reuse? I've seen connection pool reuse trigger weird classloader combos in the past. Try ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS) briefly. :thinking_face:

maria: Tried that locally. Setting maxIdleConnections=0 made the exception disappear. So it feels like a connection-level cache/keep-alive interaction.

alex: That strongly hints at a ClassLoader/ServiceLoader mismatch between two versions of Gson/Jackson on the same JVM — e.g., the shaded classes vs an unshaded copy loaded by some other library on the reused connection lifecycle. The stacktrace cast is between two gson types that should be identical but come from different classloader roots.

sam: Also remember that Gson uses reflection and some adapter factories can be cached statically by libraries or via ServiceLoader. If a connection keeps references to a parser instance created under a different classpath layout, you can get this. The usual fixes:
- Ensure only one copy of gson/jackson is visible at runtime (prefer shading + relocation)
- Avoid leaving objects with library-internal types in long-lived connection attributes
- Re-package ServiceLoader files (META-INF/services) when shading so ServiceLoader.resolve() returns relocated names

jess: Another repro tip — run the service with `-verbose:class` or an agent to see which classloader loads com.google.gson.* on the hot path.

maria: Good call. I inspected the uber-jar and found we relocated classes but didn't rewrite META-INF/services entries for a small third-party lib (http-multiplexor) that still references the original com.google.gson.* service entry. That explains why a second gson copy gets loaded on reuse.

sam: Yep — shadow plugin needs `relocate` plus `filter` for resource files OR use shadowJar `transform(ServiceFileTransformer)` to rewrite service files. For Gradle Shadow plugin: `transform(com.github.jengelman.gradle.plugins.shadow.transformers.ServiceFileTransformer)` and relocate the service entries.

alex: Actionable: 1) Add ServiceFileTransformer and a small rule to rewrite META-INF/services/com.google.gson.* 2) Add a unit/integration test that simulates persistent connections + streaming NDJSON to catch it.

maria: Filing issue now and will open a PR with the shadow transform + a reproduction test. Assigning to @sam for review.

deploy-bot: build 1968423500 pushed -> staging (kotlin-client:1.8.3-shaded). CI: tests 174/180 passed — failing tests look unrelated to shading.

maria: Thanks team — marking workaround (connectionPool=0) in the incident doc and will revert once PR merges.

alex: Also consider adding a short note in the SDK README about packaging expectations (no runtime gson on classpath outside shaded bundle) — reduces future footguns. :memo:

sam: I'll review PR today. If we can add a small integration test to the infra pipeline that runs with connection reuse enabled, we should catch regressions early.

jess: Nice root cause detective work! :party_parrot:

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kotlin-client/pull/482 — includes ServiceFileTransformer + test.

alex: Thx — will review after sam.

maria: Closing loop here once merged; leaving notes in the lib packagers guide.
